findings.claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. As a result, consuming projects that target netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get generated formatters and resolvers with no [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. The requirement asks for ALL generated code to be decorated. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0, and is valid on classes there, so the exclusion is not needed. Multi-targeting libraries lose the exclusion on those target frameworks.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageLegacyTargetsTests.GeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverageOnLegacyTargets("NETSTANDARD2_0") and ("NETFRAMEWORK"). The test runs the generator with that preprocessor symbol defined and reports every generated formatter or resolver type that lacks the attribute. Expected to fail on head. The same guard appears in EnumTemplate.tt:8, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:18, UnionTemplate.tt:10, ResolverTemplate.tt:14/31/48 and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt:7/35.

findings.claim: The README states the attribute is 'not available' on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. This is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ships in both. The docs therefore justify a coverage gap the requirement does not allow.

receipt_plan.detail: API docs for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute list it under .NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0. Compare with README.md lines 1639-1640.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always-on, with no setting. Every generated formatter and resolver class is unconditionally decorated with [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] in the T4 templates. This is what the change does, minus its target-framework #if guard.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Configurable, as the requirement says 'setting would be fine'. Add a boolean generator option (e.g. on the formatter/resolver options read by the generator, default true). The templates emit the attribute line only when that option is enabled, so users can turn the exclusion off. This needs a new option property, plumbing it into the template classes, and wrapping each emitted attribute line in a template-level `if (option)`.
